direction.premise: A small computational petri dish: construct an environment and watch a single blue learner discover its consequences.
direction.composition: The rectangular cell culture occupies the central work surface. A wrapping instrument strip sits above it and only step/reward counters sit below.
direction.shapeLanguage: Hard square cells and compact rectangular instrument buttons match the discrete world. The icon places that grid inside a circular specimen dish.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Flat opaque cell pigments retain the source renderer. Muted teal instrument metal surrounds a near-black culture surface without glass effects.
direction.paletteLogic: Blue marks the learner and spawn, green marks the goal, red the harmful cells, and yellow the rewards. Grey walls preserve legibility over a dark empty grid.
direction.typography: System sans-serif labels keep controls legible at compact sizes. The product name is a small bench label rather than a decorative title.
direction.signature: Draw an obstacle with a finger and immediately send the learner one step into the edited environment; reward changes remain visible in the bottom counter.
direction.distinction: FOG uses geographic orders and ZAMAZKA uses painted fragments; PetriForge keeps every editable element aligned to a fixed discrete laboratory grid.

architecture.primaryVerb: Paint individual cells or generator patterns, then advance or run a learner against the resulting rewards and walls.
architecture.physicalFeedback: A painted cell changes immediately and persists until undo; the agent advances in discrete steps with no interpolated movement to obscure its sampled state.
architecture.spatialRationale: The whole 30 by 20 environment remains visible when fitted to the phone width; the wrapping tool strip allows direct editing without a modal navigation stack.

comparisons.spatialDifference: fog-of-conquest uses full-bleed-world and diegetic-tools; this port shows a fitted rectangular laboratory grid with an explicit tool strip.
comparisons.interactionDifference: fog-of-conquest uses scene-zoom navigation; PetriForge exposes cell brushes, undo, procedural maps and a separately stepped learning worker.

production.renderer: Canvas 2D preserves the recovered source cell renderer and exact 30 by 20 simulation without a GPU or external assets.
production.focalAsset: The focal object is the editable cell culture drawn from source rules; a hand-authored SVG dish and cell path provide the install identity.

motion.character: Discrete and immediate: state changes occur on cell boundaries because the learner samples one action at a time.
motion.action: Painting a wall or advancing the agent is the primary visible interaction.
motion.anticipation: The selected tool and tile value expose the pending edit before the pointer touches the culture.
motion.response: Pointer input changes the cell pigment immediately; a worker action changes the blue learner position and reward counter.
motion.followThrough: Edited cells remain until an explicit undo or another paint operation; the completed episode stops the run control.
motion.interruption: Pointer cancellation releases the current stroke; repeated run input toggles execution while a single pending worker request prevents backlogs.
motion.reducedMotion: There are no decorative transitions to remove; discrete cell changes retain all simulation information.

evidence.expectedChange: The blue learner takes one discrete action and the step counter advances by exactly one.
